cls: Biologic DMARD - tumor necrosis factor (TNF-alpha) blocker
pharm: Recombinant human monoclonal antibody that binds TNF-alpha and blocks its interaction with cell-surface TNF receptors, reducing inflammation in immune-mediated diseases.
quick: Rheumatoid/psoriatic arthritis & ankylosing spondylitis: 40 mg subcutaneously every other week
Subcutaneous injection; not related to meals
Limited data; crosses placenta in 3rd trimester - affects infant live-vaccine timing
Low levels in milk; generally considered compatible
No specific dose adjustment; monitor for HBV reactivation/hepatotoxicity
No direct interaction; avoid if on methotrexate (hepatotoxicity)
TB screening before/during, infections, CBC, hepatitis B, malignancy signs
summary: Adalimumab is a recombinant human monoclonal antibody (TNF-alpha blocker) used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, and non-infectious uveitis. The usual adult arthritis dose is 40 mg subcutaneously every other week. It carries a BOXED WARNING for serious infections (including reactivation of latent tuberculosis, invasive fungal and opportunistic infections) that may be fatal, and for malignancy, including lymphoma and hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (especially in adolescents/young adults). Test for latent TB and hepatitis B before starting, and monitor closely for infection during therapy.
indications: Rheumatoid arthritis (moderately to severely active) in adults
Polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 years and older
Crohn disease (moderately to severely active) in adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older
Ulcerative colitis (moderately to severely active) in adults
Moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis in adults
Moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa in adults
Non-infectious intermediate, posterior, and panuveitis in adults

dosage.d: 40 mg every other week; some RA patients not on methotrexate may benefit from 40 mg weekly or 80 mg every other week
10-<15 kg: 10 mg; 15-<30 kg: 20 mg; >=30 kg: 40 mg - all every other week
160 mg on Day 1 (or split over 2 days), 80 mg on Day 15, then 40 mg every other week from Day 29
dosage.n: Maintenance is 40 mg every other week

dosage.d: Psoriasis: 80 mg initial then 40 mg every other week starting 1 week later; HS: 160 mg Day 1, 80 mg Day 15, then 40 mg weekly; uveitis: 80 mg initial then 40 mg every other week starting 1 week later

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection in the abdomen or thigh; rotate injection sites
Bring the prefilled syringe/pen to room temperature before injecting; do not shake; inspect for particulates
Complete latent TB screening and hepatitis B testing before the first dose
Do not give live vaccines concurrently; bring pediatric and infant vaccinations up to date before therapy
Store refrigerated; patients may self-inject after appropriate training
moa: Adalimumab is a recombinant fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and blocks its interaction with the p55 and p75 cell-surface TNF receptors. It does not bind lymphotoxin (TNF-beta). By neutralizing TNF-alpha - a key proinflammatory cytokine elevated in rheumatoid and other inflammatory diseases - it reduces inflammation, joint destruction, and disease activity, and modulates TNF-regulated adhesion molecules involved in leukocyte migration. It can also lyse surface-TNF-expressing cells in the presence of complement.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to adalimumab or any excipient (per product labeling; original labeling lists no formal contraindications)
relative: Active serious infection (including localized infection), active or latent tuberculosis, chronic/recurrent infection
Moderate to severe heart failure (NYHA III/IV)
Concurrent use of other biologic DMARDs or anakinra/abatacept (increased infection risk)
monitor: Active and latent tuberculosis before and during therapy
Complete blood count and signs of malignancy
Hepatitis B reactivation, heart failure, and neurologic symptoms

preg: There are limited data; adalimumab actively crosses the placenta during the third trimester and may affect the infant's immune response. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed; infants exposed in utero should not receive live vaccines for several months after birth.
lact: Adalimumab is present in human milk in very low concentrations and is poorly absorbed by the infant; breastfeeding is generally considered compatible. Weigh benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's need for the drug.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment; adalimumab is a monoclonal antibody not eliminated renally.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for hepatic impairment. Monitor for hepatitis B reactivation and rare hepatotoxicity, particularly with concomitant methotrexate.

major: Other TNF blockers / biologic DMARDs (e.g., anakinra, abatacept) - increased serious infection risk; do not combine
Live vaccines - avoid during therapy (risk of vaccine infection)
moderate: Immunosuppressants (methotrexate, corticosteroids) - additive infection risk (most serious infections occurred on concomitant immunosuppressants)
Drugs metabolized by CYP450 with narrow index (e.g., warfarin, cyclosporine, theophylline) - normalization of TNF on starting therapy may alter their levels
minor: No significant pharmacokinetic small-molecule interactions established
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; limit alcohol if on concomitant methotrexate due to hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Obtain tuberculin/IGRA testing and hepatitis B serologies before initiation; CBC monitoring during therapy.

serious: Serious infections including bacterial sepsis, tuberculosis (including reactivation), invasive fungal and opportunistic infections
Malignancies including lymphoma and (rare) hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma in adolescents/young adults
Demyelinating disease (multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis, Guillain-Barre)

monitoring: Test for latent TB before therapy and monitor for active TB during and after treatment
Screen for hepatitis B before therapy; monitor carriers for reactivation
Signs and symptoms of infection at every visit; discontinue for serious infection/sepsis
Complete blood count and signs of malignancy (especially lymphoma)
Heart failure status and new neurologic symptoms
counsel: This medicine lowers your immune defenses - call your doctor at the first sign of infection (fever, cough, night sweats, weight loss, persistent sore)
You will be tested for TB and hepatitis B before starting; tell your doctor if you have had TB or live in/travel to areas with fungal infections
Do not receive live vaccines while on treatment; keep your (and your child's) vaccines up to date beforehand
Learn proper subcutaneous injection technique and site rotation; store in the refrigerator and let it warm before injecting
Report numbness/tingling, vision changes, unusual bleeding/bruising, persistent fever, or new lumps
pk: Clinical improvement typically over 1-12 weeks depending on indication
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; protect from light; may store at room temp up to 14 days per labeling
pearls: BOXED WARNING: serious infections (including reactivation of latent TB, invasive fungal and opportunistic infections) that may be fatal - screen and treat latent TB before starting and monitor throughout
BOXED WARNING: malignancy, including lymphoma and rare hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (especially adolescents/young adults with Crohn/UC on thiopurines)
Screen for hepatitis B before therapy; monitor carriers for reactivation
Avoid live vaccines; avoid combining with other biologics/anakinra; caution in NYHA III/IV heart failure and demyelinating disease
Most serious infections occurred in patients also on methotrexate or corticosteroids - factor in cumulative immunosuppression
missed: If a dose is missed, inject it as soon as remembered, then take the next dose at the regularly scheduled time (do not double up). If a dose is significantly delayed, contact the prescriber for guidance on resuming the every-other-week schedule.
overdose: Doses up to 10 mg/kg have been administered in clinical trials without dose-limiting toxicities. There is no known specific antidote. In case of overdose, monitor the patient for any signs or symptoms of adverse reactions and institute appropriate symptomatic treatment.
